aiOverview.content: As of March 2026, former Real Housewives of Beverly Hills star Teddi Mellencamp is in an ongoing battle with Stage 4 melanoma, which has metastasized to her brain and lungs. Despite recent, scary complications, she has reported that her tumors have significantly shrunk or are not detectable on scans, though she is not considered in remission and continues treatment. Latest Cancer Updates (2026) No Detectable Cancer/Immunotherapy: In late 2025 and early 2026, Teddi revealed that, while she is still considered Stage 4, her scans showed "no detectable cancer" in her body following treatment. However, she remains on a strict, long-term immunotherapy regimen. March 2026 Hospitalization: In early March 2026, Teddi was hospitalized for a "rare and life-threatening" skin condition called Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), which caused painful sores all over her body and was triggered by a new medication. Mental and Physical Toll: She has spoken openly about the difficulty of the process, stating her energy levels shift by the hour. Her father, John Mellencamp, mentioned in January 2026 that she has been "suffering" from the side effects of her treatments, though Teddi later clarified this was more of a mental and emotional struggle than a return of the cancer itself. 2026 iHeartRadio Music Awards: At the March 26, 2026, awards show, she tearfully honored her father, John Mellencamp, attributing her survival to his support and intervention. Background and Journey Initial Diagnosis: Teddi was first diagnosed with Stage 2 melanoma in October 2022 after a mole on her back was checked, a spot noticed by friend and former castmate Kyle Richards. Metastasis: By February 2025, she revealed that the melanoma had spread to her brain and lungs, requiring multiple surgeries and the classification of her cancer as Stage 4. Treatment: She has undergone over a dozen surgeries and extensive rounds of immunotherapy. Personal LifeAmid her cancer journey, Teddi and her estranged husband, Edwin Arroyave, paused their divorce proceedings (announced in late 2024) to focus on her health and family. This information is based on reports through March 2026.
